editorial:
Have you ever felt like you had to hide a huge part of yourself just to be liked? That is exactly where you find Leanna. After losing all her hair to Alopecia as a young child, she grew up feeling like she had to trick the world to fit in. She becomes an expert at covering up her hair loss, but it takes a huge toll on her mental health. When she meets Terrence, everything changes. He is kind and loving, and for the first time, you see Leanna struggle with the fear of being truly seen. It is a heartfelt story that feels very real and hits close to home if you have ever dealt with insecurity.

The acting feels natural, and the chemistry between the leads makes you really root for them. While the pacing is a bit slow in some parts, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. You will love how the movie handles sensitive topics without being too dramatic. If you want to see it, I suggest renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or you can grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection if you want the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a cozy night in.
endingExplained: By the end, Leanna finally stops hiding her secret. She has a brave conversation with Terrence and reveals her hair loss, fearing he will leave her. Instead, Terrence accepts her completely and loves her for who she is, not her looks. This gives Leanna the strength to stop wearing wigs and start loving herself. The movie wraps up with her feeling free and confident in her new, honest relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about self-love and overcoming fear.
